name: Differentiable Rendering from First Principles
definition: Differentiable rendering computes the gradient of a scalar loss of the synthesized image with respect to scene parameters (e.g., camera pose, light intensity, vertex positions), enabling gradient descent to find scene parameters that render to observed images or to train neural networks with rendering losses.
summary: Differentiable rendering computes accurate gradients for scene optimization by deriving derivatives from first principles, explicitly handling occlusion discontinuities without approximation.
